findings.title: New, undocumented user-storage contract: all raw recovery codes passed as a JSON array in the credential value
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the full list of *raw* (unhashed) recovery codes into a JSON array and passes it as the challenge-response/value of a UserCredentialModel of type `recovery-authn-codes` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. This establishes a brand new, completely undocumented contract that every UserStorageProvider must now implement to receive recovery codes (the JSON encoding, the fact that the value is a list and not a single code, that the provider is responsible for hashing them and for invalidating individual codes after use). Nothing in the SPI javadoc, the UserStorage documentation, or a migration note describes it; the only example is the testsuite provider, which stores the codes in clear text and compares them with `String.equals`. Without documentation, third-party providers will either reject the update (silently falling back to local storage) or mis-store the codes. At minimum the method javadoc should specify the wire format and the provider's obligations (hashing, single-use invalidation).

findings.title: Federated-first credential lookup can disagree with credential validation order and with an existing local credential
findings.body: getCredential() returns the federated recovery-codes credential if the user storage exposes one, and only otherwise the locally stored one. A user can legitimately have both (e.g. codes were created locally before the federation provider started supporting the type, or a previous `updateCredential` returned false). In that case the login form renders the "next code number" taken from the federated model while `credentialManager().isValid()` may validate against the other credential, so the user is asked for code N but only code M is accepted, making login impossible. The helper should either take the credential from the same source that will validate it, or the creation path should delete the stale local credential when the credential is stored in the user storage.

findings.title: Unguarded Optional.get() breaks the recovery-code login form for providers that don't expose credentials
findings.body: The bean calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. A UserStorageProvider can fully support recovery codes by implementing `supportsCredentialType`/`isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` (which is what makes `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.configuredFor()` return true) while not implementing the optional `getCredentials()` method. In that case `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` returns an empty Optional and rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException, producing an HTTP 500 error page instead of a login form. Since this PR makes federated recovery codes a supported scenario, this path is now reachable in a supported configuration and must degrade gracefully (or the requirement to implement getCredentials must be enforced/documented).

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById() is called with a federated credential id
findings.body: After the lookup was switched to `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, the credential returned here may come from the user storage (federated) instead of the local credential store. The code then calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only operates on the local store, so for a federated credential the call silently does nothing (and the id may even be null, as it is for the testsuite provider which rebuilds the model with `createFromValues`). Consequence: when a federated provider reports all codes as used, the exhausted credential is never removed and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action will be re-added on every subsequent login, leaving the user in a loop. The removal/reset needs to be delegated to the user storage (e.g. via disableCredentialType/updateCredential) when the credential is federated.

findings.title: getCredentials() dereferences a possibly null MyUser
findings.body: `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` can return null (getMyUser is a plain map lookup by username, and every other method in this class — isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isValid — explicitly null-checks it). `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 then throws NullPointerException whenever getCredentials is invoked for a user that is no longer in the in-memory map (e.g. after removeUser, or for a stale cached UserModel), which will surface as a 500 in account/admin endpoints that list credentials and make tests flaky. Add the null check and return Stream.empty().

findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential is rebuilt on every call, losing id and used-code state
findings.body: getCredentials() builds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` from the raw codes on each invocation. The returned model therefore has no id and always reports every code as unused, and the provider never marks a code as consumed in isValid(). As a result this reference provider models recovery codes as infinitely reusable, the credential cannot be addressed by id (account console delete, removeStoredCredentialById), and the new test cannot detect a regression in the single-use semantics of recovery codes.

findings.title: New test only covers one successful login; no coverage of code consumption, wrong code, or fallback to local storage
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only sets up codes and performs a single successful login with code #0. It does not verify that the used code is rejected on a second login / that the form then asks for the next code, does not verify that an invalid code is rejected, does not assert that no credential leaked into the local DB *after* the login, and does not cover the other branch of the new code in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (a federated user whose storage does not support `recovery-authn-codes`, which must fall back to the local credential store). The two behaviours this PR is about — storing in user storage and falling back to local — are therefore only half covered.

findings.title: Unneeded 'delayed-authenticator' execution (with typo'd config alias) added to the test browser flow
findings.body: configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes adds a REQUIRED `delayed-authenticator` execution with delay 0 and a config alias typo ("delayed-suthenticator-config"). The delay serves no purpose for this test, but it makes the flow (and the test) depend on an extra testsuite authenticator being deployed and on the `delay` config being accepted; if that provider is unavailable the flow fails at authentication time for reasons unrelated to recovery codes. The parameter and the execution should be dropped (or at least the alias typo fixed).
